result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A uses one 4px spacing scale throughout, and its tinted, borderless filter strip clearly sets the filters apart from the white schedule surface. Answer B mixes spacing values (3, 6, 10, 14px) and draws the filters, schedule and summary as identical bordered panels, so the groups are less distinct and the inner edges don't quite line up (12px vs 14px padding). B adds working filters and dark mode, but those aren't on the rubric. Both separate the summary with only a light 1px border and give the rows comfortable 44px heights. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B uses an explicit 4px spacing scale, and its tinted filter strip clearly sets the filters apart from the white schedule surface. A uses mixed spacing values (3, 6, 10 and 14px) and gives the filters the same white panel as the schedule. A has working room and engineer filters, but both answers do equally well on row padding and summary separation, and B is slightly more consistent on edge alignment.
